name: FARLEY, David

headline.note: A long private-sector agribusiness career is documented, but sources do not establish substantive full-time status and exact non-overlapping boundaries for the entire sequence. Executive titles are not treated as proof of full-time work. Governance, advocacy, campaigning and elected office are excluded; missing evidence is not zero.

career_spells.role: Jackaroo, later overseer, station manager and irrigation development specialist
career_spells.evidence_note: The current party biography supplies the employer and role progression; a March 2026 local interview gives a 1975 start and says he moved from jackaroo through overseer and irrigation-development work before the northern NSW appointment. Exact role-transition and cessation dates, employment entity, hours and leave are unresolved.
career_spells.counting_note: Private employment is supported, but year-only boundaries and absent substantive full-time evidence do not establish an exact countable interval.

career_spells.role: Farm manager and operational leadership roles
career_spells.evidence_note: First-party and local reporting place his appointment to develop the northern NSW irrigation enterprise in 1982, while the public professional-profile search result says he joined Colly Cotton as farm manager in 1983. The profile says promotion to managing director/CEO occurred in 1990. The one-year start conflict, legal employing entity, exact dates, hours and leave are unresolved.
career_spells.counting_note: Private employment is supported, but conflicting year-level evidence and absent substantive full-time evidence preclude an exact total.

career_spells.role: Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer
career_spells.evidence_note: The public profile records promotion in 1990. The party biography describes more than two decades at the enterprise, while the local interview says 19 years; neither establishes a precise cessation date. The senior titles are not treated as proof of full-time work.
career_spells.counting_note: Private employment is supported, but the end date and full-time status are insufficient for an exact headline calculation.

career_spells.evidence_note: The party biography and local interview identify leadership of the California cotton cooperative between Colly Cotton and AACo. Contemporary industry material identifies him as Calcot's fifth CEO and first external appointment. Exact commencement, cessation, employment status, hours and any Matrix overlap remain unresolved.
career_spells.counting_note: The cooperative executive role is private-sector employment, but its dates and substantive full-time status are not sufficiently established.

career_spells.role: Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer
career_spells.evidence_note: The party biography identifies the role. ABC Rural reports that he joined as CEO in December 2009 and that his departure was announced on 30 July 2013. The exact December start day, employment contract, hours and leave are unresolved; the senior title is not treated as proof of full-time work.
career_spells.counting_note: Private employment and month/day boundaries are supported, but substantive full-time status is not directly evidenced.

career_spells.role: Executive Chairman; agricultural commodity trader, investor and consultant
career_spells.evidence_note: The public professional-profile search result gives Executive Chairman from April 2020; the company site describes investment, commodity trading and agribusiness consulting, and NSW parliamentary records identify him in that role in June 2025. March 2026 reporting says he still operated the company. The 9 May 2026 endpoint marks election, not a proven business cessation; pre-April 2020 Matrix involvement, hours, leave and continuing post-election work are unresolved.
career_spells.counting_note: A private self-employed/business role is supported, but hours and the relationship between election and continuing business activity are unresolved.

career_spells.evidence_note: The public professional-profile search result supplies the month-level dates and describes the position as investor and executive director. Duties, remuneration, hours and overlap with Matrix are unresolved, so this is retained as governance/investment rather than assumed substantive employment.
career_spells.counting_note: Governance/investment is excluded absent evidence that it was substantive full-time employment.

career_spells.evidence_note: March 2026 local reporting identifies him as current chair. Appointment dates, legal entity, remuneration, hours and overlap with Matrix and campaigning are unresolved; a chair title is not assumed to be paid employment.
career_spells.counting_note: Advocacy/governance is excluded from public/private headline totals.

career_spells.evidence_note: Secondary reporting records preselection on 7 March 2026 and election on 9 May 2026. Campaign remuneration, hours, Matrix leave and overlap are unresolved.
career_spells.counting_note: Party campaigning is excluded under the codebook.

career_spells.evidence_note: The frozen roster and election reporting establish House service from the 9 May 2026 by-election. Whether Matrix or other private activities continued after election is unresolved.
career_spells.counting_note: Elected office is excluded under the codebook.

research_notes: The frozen official record contains no occupation text, so this initial record relies on a current party biography, primary company/government material, a public professional profile and reported interviews.
The 1982/1983 Colly commencement conflict is preserved rather than silently resolved; relative duration is not converted into an invented cessation date.
Executive titles are not treated as proof of substantive full-time work, so no private headline total is calculated despite extensive documented private-sector experience.
Company, board and advocacy overlaps are kept separate; the election date is not assumed to terminate private business activity.
open_questions: What were the legal employing entities, exact dates, hours and leave for F.S. Falkiner and each Colly Cotton role?
Did Colly Cotton commence in 1982 or 1983, and when precisely did the CEO role end?
What were the exact Calcot appointment and cessation dates, employment terms and Matrix overlap?
Can AACo personnel or remuneration records establish substantive full-time status and the exact December 2009 start day?
When did Farley first begin paid work through Matrix, and what were his hours, ownership, client engagements and AACo/board/campaign overlaps?
Did Matrix work continue after election, and what leave or cessation arrangements applied?
Were Waverley Mills and Speak Up 4 Water roles paid substantive employment or governance only?
